answer: Cap every newcomer at a narrow inlet: a fresh identity may move only a trickle of value, and the channel widens through months of honest work — no shortcut buys that history. A farmer minting ten thousand clones gains nothing, because each clone queues at the same thin opening; the farm's total throughput is throttled by time served, not by names printed. Cracking a walnut takes steady pressure, not one blow, and a falcon earns its range by flying it: reputation here accrues day by day. Limit: a patient farm can eventually graduate its clones, so quotas must decay while an identity sits idle.
